units.title: 1. Definitions, Semiology and Pseudo Seizure
units.guide:
Semiology is the signs and symptoms of seizure activity; seizure is transient excessive hypersynchronous neuronal activity.
Motor activity is ordered fastest to slowest from myoclonic to atonic, and pseudo seizure has adolescent, attention-seeking and pupillary clues.

units.title: 2. Classification (ILAE 2017), Focal and Generalized Onset
units.guide:
ILAE 2017 classification is based on onset into focal, generalized and unknown, with LOC awareness subdividing focal.
Focal motor and non-motor tables separate complex partial impaired awareness with automatisms from simple partial motor types, and generalized onset splits into motor GTCS and non-motor absence.

units.title: 3. Epilepsy Evaluation and Focal Seizures
units.guide:
Epilepsy work-up evaluates MRI, EEG, type of onset and LOC to predict further seizure risk and determine syndrome.
Focal seizures are compared without vs with dyscognition: simple partial aware vs complex partial with LOC, post-ictal disorientation and medial temporal localization, with structural frontal lesions irritating opposite brain.

units.title: 4. Focal Presentation, Investigations and Medial Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
units.sec: Focal Seizure Presentation and Medial Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
units.guide:
Without dyscognition presentation is tonic > tonic clonic > sensory flashing light/autonomic with 2-3 Hz clonic, Todd's palsy up to 24h, Jacksonian march distal to proximal and epilepsia partialis continua hours to days.
With dyscognition has abdominal aura fullness->regurgitation > visual > auditory, behavioural arrest motionless stare, automatisms lip smacking chewing and anterograde amnesia, with MRI hippocampal sclerosis, EEG temporal spikes and lifelong AED for with dyscognition.

units.title: 5. Generalized Seizures and Typical Childhood Absence
units.guide:
MRI T2 flare and T1 flare point to hippocampal sclerosis with temporal lobe spikes on EEG, while normal EEG is also shown.
Typical childhood absence is non-motor with sudden brief lapse, no postural loss, absent post-ictal confusion, IQ normal, pause/stare > automatisms > eye movement, hyperventilation aggravation, normal MRI and 3Hz spike-wave, treated till 12 with valproate preferred and ethosuximide.

units.title: 6. Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy, Myoclonic and Atonic Seizures
units.guide:
Juvenile myoclonic epilepsy presents 6-25 years female > male with sleep deprivation upon awakening, GTCS 90% and absence 1/3, very short LOC, shock-like myoclonus face-trunk-upper limb > lower limb.
Atonic seizures are sudden loss of muscle tone in children, associated with Lennox Gastaut syndrome tonic > atonic > drop attacks > absent, with mental retardation, refractory epilepsy and slow spike-wave background; Lennox is not associated with myoclonic seizures.
